links.comparator_used: Pre-optimization version of Xiaoyi (initial system) evaluated in a first round of 1000 sessions, versus the post-optimization version in a second round of 1000 sessions. The optimization bundled prompt revision with knowledge-base and tool expansion and validation rules, so the prompt effect is not isolated.
links.outcome: Session-level overall quality and clinical appropriateness, and turn-level deficiency rate, rated by 40 pediatricians
links.effect: Good overall quality 652 (65.2%) to 743 (74.3%); clinically appropriate 614 (61.4%) to 874 (87.4%), both P<.001; turn-level deficiency 19.4% (790/4073) to 6.9% (236/3419), OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.24-0.37, P<.001
links.tradeoff: Deficiencies persisted after optimization, and suboptimal clinical recommendations (not tailored to the child's age or clinical context) remained the most frequent category. The authors say continued monitoring and refinement are needed.
links.quote: The turn-level deficiency rate declined from 19.4% (790/4073 turns) to 6.9% (236/3419 turns; odds ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.24-0.37; P<.001), with suboptimal clinical recommendations (not optimally tailored to the child's age or clinical context) remaining the most frequent category.

design_hint: expert-guided optimization including prompt revision, knowledge-base expansion, and validation rules
